section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section explores how body image-related cognitive fusion and body appreciation mediate the impact of body image discrepancy on disordered eating behaviors, while controlling for BMI. The findings of the present study corroborate existing literature, showing positive associations between BMI, body image discrepancy, and eating psychopathology. The study, which used a sample exclusively composed of women from the general population, found that negative body image perception directly explains disordered eating behaviors, and its impact is also mediated by increased cognitive fusion and decreased body appreciation. Limitations include the cross-sectional nature of the study, the exclusive use of a female sample, and the reliance on self-report measures.
